title: Full vs Incremental Loads in ETL

scenes.say: If your dataset keeps growing, should you reload everything each time, or just process what's new?
A full load replaces all data every run—simple, but wasteful for big tables. Incremental loads only pick up new or changed records, so they're much more efficient.

rows.b: Use a watermark like updated time
Select only new or changed rows

scenes.say: To run an incremental load, first track changes with a watermark, then filter for new records, and finally append them to your target.

scenes.label: Watermark
scenes.sub: A marker that tracks the latest processed record
scenes.say: A watermark is just a marker—like the latest timestamp—so you know where you left off.

scenes.question: Should you always use full loads?
scenes.right: No. For large datasets, incremental loads save time and resources.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: always using full loads. That wastes compute and bandwidth on big data. Incremental loading is the scalable choice.
